career_ladder.note: Officers directly recruited through the Delhi Higher Judicial Service (DHJS) enter the Senior Judicial Cadre of the National Capital Territory of Delhi as Additional District and Sessions Judges under the Delhi Higher Judicial Service Rules, 1970. They preside over serious criminal trials, commercial disputes, and appellate civil jurisdictions, with direct eligibility for elevation as Judges of the High Court of Delhi under Article 217(2)(a) of the Constitution of India.

exam_scheme.note: The Delhi Higher Judicial Service Examination comprises three rigorous successive stages: Preliminary Examination (Objective type with negative marking), Main Examination (Written Descriptive comprising 4 substantive papers), and Viva-Voce (Oral Interview before a Bench of Hon'ble High Court Judges) pursuant to the DHJS Rules, 1970.

papers.qualifying_threshold: 50% marks for General Category, 45% for SC, ST and PwD candidates

Paper IV — Law - III (Criminal Jurisprudence: CrPC, IPC, Indian Evidence Act, POCSO Act, Prevention of Corruption Act, NDPS Act)

financial_package.note: Higher Judicial Service officers are placed on the revised pay scale of the Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) at Level J-5 with an initial basic pay of ₹1,44,840. In addition to 58% Dearness Allowance, officers are provided designated judicial accommodation (bungalows/flats in judicial officer enclaves), sumptuary allowance, robe allowance, official staff, and comprehensive medical coverage.
financial_package.pay_source_label: High Court of Delhi — DHJS Rules, 1970 read with SNJPC Pay Matrix Notification
financial_package.estimate_note: Calculations based on entry basic pay of ₹1,44,840 + 58% DA (₹84,007) + allowances (Sumptuary Allowance ₹2,500, Orderly Allowance, Medical, and 27% HRA if official judicial housing is not occupied). In-hand estimate accounts for 10% NPS deductions, income tax TDS, and judicial welfare subscriptions.
official_perks: Official designated judicial bungalow / Type VI residential quarter in prime central Delhi judicial colonies
Dedicated air-conditioned courtroom, private judicial chamber, and stenographic personal staff
Sumptuary Allowance, Robe Allowance, and Law Books & Journals Annual Grant
Residential peon / orderly facility and driver allowance
Official staff car / vehicle facility or dedicated conveyance allowance
Free residential telephone, mobile device reimbursement, and high-speed broadband connection
Cashless medical treatment and comprehensive hospitalization coverage under Delhi Government Employees Health Scheme (DGEHS)
